about_book: High performance concrete (HPC) can be defined as the concrete, which meetsrnspecial performance and uniformity requirements that can't always be achievedrnby conventional materials, normal mixing, placing and curing practices. Thernrequirements may involve enhancements of characteristics such as placementrnand compaction without segregation, long-term mechanical properties, early-agernstrength, volume stability or service live in severe environments. Swamy statesrnthat High performance concrete (HPC) is that which is designed to givernoptimised performance characteristics for the given set of materials, usage andrnexposure conditions, consistent with requirements of cost, service life andrndurability. Architects, engineers and constructors all over the world are findingrnthat using HPC allows them to build more durable structures at comparable cost.rnHPC is being used for buildings in aggressive environments, marine structures,rnhighway bridges and pavements, nuclear structures, tunnels, precast units, etc.rnThe major difference between conventional concrete and HPC is essentially thernuse of chemical and mineral admixtures. Use of chemical admixtures reduces thernwater content, thereby reducing the porosity within the hydrated cement paste.rnPozzolanic materials are crucial to HPC as far as flowability is concerned.rnMineral admixtures, also called as cement replacement materials, act asrnpozzolanic materials as well as fine fillers, thereby the microstructure ofrnhardened cement matrix becomes denser and stronger.rnFly ash has been used in blended cements, and it has been used successfully tornreplace Portland cement up to 30% by mass as pozzolanic materials in HPC.rnBecause fly ash causes environmental pollution and the cost of storage of fly ashrnis very high, the utilization of fly ash in concrete technology, both in regard tornenvironmental pollution and the positive effect on a country's economy arernbeyond dispute. The fly ash HPC system offers a holistic approach that can helprnus to achieve the goals of meeting the rising demands for concrete, enhancementrnof concrete durability with little or no increase in cost (in some instances reducedrncost), and ecological disposal of large quantities of the solid waste products fromrncoal-fired power plants. Several laboratory and field investigations reported thatrnHPC containing fly ash had exhibited excellent mechanical and durabilityrnproperties. Despite the benefits of fly ash, practical problems remain in fieldrnapplication. At early stages of aging, the strength of HPC containing a highrnvolume of fly ash as a partial cement replacement is much lower than that ofrncontrol concrete, due to the slow process of the pozzolanic reaction of fly ash, andrnits contribution towards the strength development occurs only at later ages.rnDifferent approaches have been used to accelerate the pozzolanic reaction of flyrnash and, thereby, to increase the early strength of HPC containing fly ash. Thernactivators have been used to improve the unsatisfactory early properties ofrnPortland cement paste with fly ash added as a cement replacement.
